cards.text: Zechariah the prophet has been seeing vision after vision, with an angel right there helping him understand them. Now he lifts up his eyes AGAIN. Something is coming out from between two mountains.

cards.question: What does Zechariah see coming out from between the two mountains?

cards.text: And these aren't regular mountains. I spent YEARS staring at dust in a junk drawer, and Zechariah gets mountains of BRONZE. Not jealous, friend, just saying.
Each chariot has its own team of horses. Red horses, black horses, white horses and dappled horses.

cards.question: Zechariah says only the white horses are strong.

cards.text: Four chariots. Four colors. ZERO explanation. Good thing the angel who's been speaking with Zechariah is standing right there.

cards.question: Zechariah is looking at four chariots he doesn't understand. What does he do?

answers.text: Asks the angel what they are

cards.text: Zechariah asks, "What are these, my lord?" The angel tells him they are the four spirits of heaven.

cards.question: The angel says the four spirits of heaven are going forth. Where are they going forth from?

answers.text: Their station before the Lord of all the earth
The gates of the temple in Jerusalem
A house built in the land of Shinar

cards.text: Then the angel hands out directions like a delivery dispatcher. The dappled horses? South.

cards.question: The angel says the black horses go toward the land of the ___, and the white horses go toward the ___.
The angel also tells Zechariah that the red horses are headed east.

cards.text: These strong horses are EAGER to go. Like me when the oven timer dings, and I've singed my mustache twice racing to get there first.

cards.question: The horses are eager to go, but the LORD tells them to wait at the mountains a little longer.

cards.text: Instead the LORD says, "Go and patrol the earth." And off they go. They patrol the earth.

cards.question: Then the LORD summons Zechariah with news about the ones going to the land of the ___.
What does the LORD say the ones who went to the land of the north have done there?

answers.text: Brought back word from the kings

cards.text: The LORD says, "Behold, those going to the land of the north have given rest to My Spirit in the land of the north." And with that, the four chariots are out patrolling the earth.

findings.problem: The card states Bible facts from outside the passage: Zechariah has been seeing vision after vision, with an angel helping him understand them (Zechariah 1-5). It cites only Zechariah 6:1 and gives no reference for that earlier context.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card is a bare list of horse colors with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads as stripped down, not as a storyteller's moment.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The setup line ("Good thing the angel who's been speaking with Zechariah is standing right there") points straight at the answer to card 7, "Asks the angel what they are." This rules out the other two answers before the baker chooses.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "The angel hands out directions" makes it sound like the angel is sending or commanding the chariots. In Zechariah 6:6 the angel is only telling Zechariah where each chariot is going. The card renames what the angel does.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The comparison "like a delivery dispatcher" has a dispatcher assigning routes. The angel only explains where the chariots are going, so the joke's action doesn't match the fact.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The blanks take compass directions ("land of the ___", "toward the ___"). The wrong answers "Egypt" and "Shinar" are place names, not directions, and neither fits either blank grammatically. That leaves "east" as the only real distractor.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card goes straight from card 15 to a blank about which land Zechariah 6:8 mentions. Nothing earlier sets up verse 8, so the baker is left guessing the next word of the line.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: No story card gives context for what the LORD says in Zechariah 6:8. The baker has to guess the wording "given rest to My Spirit" when the card should be asking about the meaning of the vision.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Most choice cards are discovery or luck questions with no reasoning setup: card 2 (what comes out), card 5 (strength), card 11 (directions), card 12 (red horses), card 16 (which land) and card 17 (what was done). Only cards 7, 9 and 14 can really be reasoned out. The stop also asks mostly about details like colors and directions, not about what the vision's picture means.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card re-quotes Zechariah 6:8, which card 17 just covered, and repeats the patrolling from card 15. It moves nothing forward.
The card tells the patrolling from Zechariah 6:7 ("the four chariots are out patrolling the earth") but cites only Zechariah 6:8. The citation should be Zechariah 6:7-8.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
